stem.en:
Kabir attacks, four times. Answer each.

Attack one: "Same atoms, same grips, same reaction. Books I to III found nothing. Your loop is made of the same stuff as the flame."

text.en: "Yes. The difference was never in the stuff. It is in the arrangement: a wall, steps, a load, a tape. Book III's own short-circuit lesson found the first crack: a flame is a battery with a bare wire."
"The seed has nitrogen and phosphorus, which the flame lacks."

feedback.en: The boiled seed has both and is dead. The Prologue's card rules that out.

text.en: "The seed's reaction is different because it is slower."

feedback.en: Same equation, same fall, from the peanut. The staircase is what makes it slow, and the staircase is the arrangement.

image.alt: Kabir's first Epilogue attack, arguing the loop is made of the same stuff as the flame, gesturing at the completed nine-line ledger page.
